title: Token Velocity Credit Mosaic
content:
Super rough brain-dump — trying to collect heuristics that might be useful for a hybrid credits model that mixes token-based metering with session/throughput allowances. This is intentionally noisy.

Goal: cheap & predictable for low-volume interactive apps (chatty), still capture high token-velocity usage from embeddings/long-doc gen.

Core ideas (short):
- Two currency model: tokens (fine-grained) + session credits (amortize latency/SLO, warm KV cache).
- Sessions buy a baseline of throughput + ephemeral cache benefits (prefix hits) — reduces marginal token cost for chatty users.
- Token buckets still apply for large/rare bursts (embedding jobs or long generations).

Back-of-envelope numbers (baseline assumptions):
- GPU infra blended cost (hosted) per GPU-hour: $3.50 (mix of A100/RTX -> blended).
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU under average chat load: 12k tok/s (inference p50 across models we serve).
- So naive GPU-hour -> tokens: 12k * 3600 = ~43M tokens/hour. Cost per million tokens = 3.50 / 43 = ~$0.081 /M tokens. (call it $0.08 for round numbers)

But this misses batching & cache: realistic effective cost for chatty small-turn workloads is ~3-6x cheaper because of batching + KV reuse. So for chatty: unit cost ~ $0.02/M tokens on average. For embeddings/long single-pass jobs (no reuse), unit cost maybe $0.12-$0.15/M.

Session credit math (sketch):
- Idea: 1 session credit = 30 minutes of active-ish usage, includes warm cache value. Could be amortized to e.g. 10k baseline tokens free-ish (subsidized) + preferential batching slot.
- Example: charge 1 credit = $0.20. If credit yields 10k tokens effective value, that's $0.02/M tokens equivalent (cheap). But if user consumes 100k tokens in that session (long gen), then the marginal tokens billed at token rates (higher).

Design knobs to tune:
- session_duration (minutes), baseline_tokens_included, token_rate_when_in_session (discount), burst_token_rate (for large generations), concurrency_slots (how many parallel outstanding calls session can get), idle_decay (credit decay if idle > X mins).

Sensible default tiers (sketch):
- Free dev: 3 session credits / month (auto-expire 30d), token cap 50k / month, limited concurrency 2. Good for interactive experiments.
- Starter (PAYG-friendly): $20/mo -> 100 session credits + 1M tokens included at dev-rate. Rolling balance.
- Scale: committed reserved pool: monthly commit maps to discounted session credit price and lower per-token marginal. Dedicated customers map to reserved GPU-hours (different pricing).

Edge cases to watch:
- Abuse: small sessions that repeatedly reconnect to get cheap baseline tokens. Need minimum active-turn threshold to qualify for session discount (e.g., >=3 RPCs or >=2s of decode).
- Background workers that spin up many sessions to farm concurrency. Cap sessions per API key and require auth/cert checks for higher concurrency.
- Multitenant sharing of sessions across users -> avoid accidental cross-billing by scoping credits to API key or sub-organization.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to instrument "cache warmness" metric? Practical proxy: percent of tokens served from KV/prefix hit or average batch size per request within session window. Need telemetry flag in runtime to report hit-rate by session-id.
- Where do we draw commit lines for Dedicated vs session-credits? Workload classifier (chatty vs batch) could auto-route and surface recommended commit.
- UX: show customers "session credit burn" timeline and equivalence to token dollars (help them reason about migration).

Quick worked example (conservative):
- Customer A: chat app, 5k DAU, avg 4 turns/session, avg 80 tokens per turn -> per session tokens = 320. If we give 150 session credits / month ($30), that's baseline capacity for 48k sessions (~3M tokens monthly) effectively at cheap rate. Marginal tokens beyond baseline billed at $0.08/M (or less if warm).
- Customer B: document summarization (batch), single job = 1M tokens, sessions not helpful. They pay pure token rate (e.g., $0.12/M) or buy reserved throughput if repeated.

Metrics to monitor post-experiment:
- average tokens/session, median batch size within session, % sessions qualifying for discount, churn vs session-credit price, abuse signals (rapid open/close), per-key concurrency distribution.

Implementation notes / runtime hooks needed:
- session-id propagated in headers, traceable to billing. Runtime exposes per-session stats: total_tokens, prefix_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, start/end timestamps.
- billing service needs to reconcile session credits daily and fallback to token billing for excess.

Thoughts on product messaging: "Sessions are your chat credit — they keep the model warm, prioritize throughput, and make chat cheaper at scale." Emphasize that heavy long-generation workloads will still be billed by tokens (no unlimited hidden risk).

Final: this is a sketch for an experiment. Next steps: instrument prefix_hit_rate, simulate 30 days of sample traffic using our trace corpus (PLAT-942) to estimate break-even points for session price and baseline token inclusions.

Notes to self: link sample traces -> CONFLUENCE-PRICING-TRACES, propose A/B in EU1 region first (cheaper infra) so we can iterate price quickly.

-- Ava
